key: Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey. With hymn sublime soliciting your favour Kusika’s son hath called unto the River.
s: Answering the rivers, who ask what the singer wants of streams that cannot halt, the seer presses his request; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.33.5, takes the request as made for the Soma he will procure once across, and ‘the River’ as the Sutudri before him.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.33.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 360653 (2022)

opened.locator: commentary on 3.33.5, and the hymn introduction

evidence.words: तद्वत्यो हे नद्यो यूयं मे विश्वामित्रस्य मम सोम्याय। उत्तीर्याहं सोमं संपादयामीत्येवं सोमसंपादिने। वचसे तदर्थमेवैः। पंचम्यर्थे तृतीया। शीघ्रगमनेभ्यो मुहूर्तं मुहूर्तमात्रमुप रमध्वं । उपपूर्वो रमिरुपसंहारे वर्तते । क्षणमात्रं शीघ्रगमनादुपरता भवत । सामान्येन नदीषुच्यमानासु समीहितं प्रयोजनमकुर्वतीषु पुरोवर्तिनीं शुतुद्रीं प्रति ब्रूते । कुशिकस्य राजर्षेः सूनुर्विश्वामित्रोऽहं बृहती महत्या मनीषा मनीषया स्तुत्यावस्युरात्मनो रक्षणमिच्छन् सन् सिंधु शुतुद्रीं त्वामच्छाभिमुख्येन प्राह्वे।
evidence.gloss: O rivers possessed of water, you: to my speech, somyāya, the speech of me, Viśvāmitra, that procures Soma, as when I say: having crossed over, I shall procure the Soma. Stop for a moment only from your swift going. When the rivers, addressed all together, do not do what he wishes, he speaks to the Śutudrī that lies before him: I, Viśvāmitra, son of the royal sage Kuśika, with great praise, desiring protection for myself, call to the river, the Śutudrī, to thee, facing thee.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 3.33.5, at [266,5]). Sāyaṇa on 3.33.5 glosses somyāya as Soma-procuring speech, spelled out as having crossed over I shall procure the Soma, and says that when the rivers addressed together do not comply he speaks to the Śutudrī before him, glossing sindhu as the Śutudrī; Wilson notes 1 and 2 report the same, and that Yāska agrees (Nir. 2.25). Plain sense faithful: 3.33.4 is the rivers’ reply asking what the singer wants, their flood not to be stayed, and 3.33.5 is the seer’s renewed request; it repeats no four words of the key verse. Revision 360653 dated 2022-11-23 by the Wikisource API, so the src year stands. Evidence copied from the packet including the source’s own spellings. entry-check ok.
